findings.finding: API key is documented as a query parameter (?api_key=...), but the live API rejects that usage and requires the X-API-Key request header.
Login response is documented with a token field, but the live API returns access_token.
Access token expiry is documented as 86400 seconds, but the live login response reports expires_in=900 seconds.
Documentation says there is no refresh flow, but the live API provides POST /auth/refresh.
The refresh token is not documented in the login response, but the live response includes refresh_token and refresh_url.
Documentation implies logout invalidates the current token server-side, but /auth/logout states tokens are stateless and the previously issued access token remained usable after logout.
Collections are documented as page/limit based with page_size in the response, but the live listings response uses offset, count and has_more.
The documented page parameter is ignored for listings: page=2&limit=20 returned the same starting records as the initial request.
The documented listings maximum limit of 200 is incorrect. limit=200 returned an effective limit/count of 50.
Listings document sort_by and order, but order=asc and order=desc returned the same ordering; descending sorting is not functioning as documented.
Seven listing records have floor values greater than total_floors, which is internally inconsistent property data.
Money is documented as INR integers, but a negative listing price was observed. Full extraction identified the corrupt records separately.
The documented GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar endpoint returned 404 for valid listing IDs.

Project documentation references /v1/listings?project_id=... for validating project listing counts, but project_id did not filter the listings response; different project IDs returned the same unfiltered result.
Rentals are documented as page/limit based with page_size, but the live rentals response uses offset, count and has_more.
The documented rentals page parameter is ignored: page=2&limit=20 returned the same starting records as the initial request.
The documented rentals maximum limit of 200 is incorrect; the effective maximum is 50.
Rentals document sort_by and order, but descending ordering is unavailable; sorting is effectively ascending only.
Projects are documented as page/limit based with page_size, but the live projects response uses offset, count and has_more.
The documented projects maximum limit of 200 is incorrect; the effective maximum is 50.
Projects document sort_by and order, but descending ordering does not work as documented; sorting is effectively ascending only.
Project price data contains anomalous records where price_min exceeds price_max. Examples include P30033-P30037.

The documented /v1/favourites endpoints (GET, POST and DELETE) returned 404. During further API investigation, the running API was found to expose the working /v1/saved endpoint, which is used by the frontend for fetching, adding and removing saved listings.
The documented GET /v1/analytics/summary endpoint returned 404 Not Found.
The listings metadata reported total=3488, but offset pagination reached 3800 retrievable records. The final page at offset 3790 contained 10 records with has_more=false.
A detailed physical-property fingerprint using property-defining attributes produced 3800 unique fingerprints for 3800 listings, with no duplicate groups.
Seven strong fake-listing candidates were identified because their positive price was below 1% of the median price for comparable listings in the same locality and bedroom category.

Project total_listings disagrees with counts derived from the complete extracted listings dataset for 317 projects. Comparing only live listings produced 95 mismatches, so all listings were used for the assignment answer.

Project price fields are inconsistent with listing-level prices. P30175 has project price_max=3.08 while its maximum listing price is ₹28,200,000, so the costliest-project answer was derived from listing prices.
